ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, terminal X is at the upper right, and terminal Y is at the lower right. The upper branch leading to X contains a voltage source labeled 2.5 V, and a series resistor labeled 2.5 Ω is connected on its left side. At the lower left there is also an active branch containing a 5 Ω resistor and a 5 V voltage source, connected to the bottom Y reference line. Some passive 5 Ω resistor branches can also be seen in the figure. Reasoning: According to the specified method, transform the two active “voltage source + series resistor” branches respectively into Norton current sources. The Norton current of the upper branch is 2.5 V / 2.5 Ω = 1 A. The Norton current of the lower-left branch is 5 V / 5 Ω = 1 A. From the source polarities in the figure, these two Norton current sources drive current in the same direction at the X-Y port, so adding them gives the Norton equivalent source current: 1 A + 1 A = 2.0 A.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the two active source-plus-series-resistor branches feeding the X-Y port: the upper 2.5 V source with 2.5 Ω, and the lower-left 5 V source with 5 Ω. Convert each branch to its Norton form: 2.5 V / 2.5 Ω = 1 A and 5 V / 5 Ω = 1 A. Since their polarities drive current in the same direction at the X-Y port, add the currents to get the Norton equivalent source current, 1 A + 1 A = 2.0 A.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses direct source-transformation rather than solving node voltages or short-circuit current equations; it identifies independent Thevenin branches in the drawing and combines their Norton current contributions.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit topology and labels from the image: terminals X and Y are the output port; there is a 2.5 V source associated with a 2.5 Ω series resistor path, and a 5 V source associated with a 5 Ω series resistor path. The remaining 5 Ω resistors are passive shunt/load branches across the same node pair and affect Norton resistance but not the algebraic source-current contribution. The source polarities in the diagram make the two Norton current contributions aid each other.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to determine the requested quantity: the Norton equivalent source current, expressed in amperes, as seen into terminals X and Y.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply the source-transformation rule: a voltage source V in series with resistance R is equivalent to a Norton current source I_N = V/R in parallel with R. Parallel Norton current sources connected with the same polarity add algebraically. Thus the contributions are 2.5/2.5 = 1 A and 5/5 = 1 A, giving total Norton source current 2 A.
